steps.text: Place potatoes in a saucepan; fill with enough water to cover potatoes. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low and cook potatoes until tender but not mushy, about 15 to 20 minutes. Drain potatoes in a colander; transfer to a baking sheet lined with a clean dish towel and allow to cool and dry out a little, about 10 minutes.
While potatoes are cooling, mix olive oil, balsamic vinegar, butter, garlic, rosemary, sage, thyme, savory, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place cooled potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Use a potato masher or the heel of your hand to lightly press down on potatoes to crush them.
Spoon the oil-herb mixture over each smashed potato.
Bake potatoes in the preheated oven until crispy, about 25 minutes. Let cool slightly before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Crispy Smashed Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Smashed potatoes are super easy to make with tender small potatoes; simply smash, season, and bake until golden and perfectly crispy on the outside.

video.description: Join us in the kitchen as we reveal the secrets to achieving golden, crunchy exteriors with tender, flavorful insides. Elevate your side dish game and savor the irresistible taste of these crispy smashed potatoes.

review.reviewBody: A Good Recipe. My variation is as follows: After draining and cooling the potatoes a little, I tumble them in bowl with a little butter to coat the skins. Instead of then 'smashing' the potatos, I cut a cross in the upper side of each, to about half-way through. Then, by using a finger and thumb on each hand to genyly squeeze in the lower half, (press between each cut line) the potato opens up, like a flower! This allows the seasoning liquid to flavour the inside of the potato more and, (if you don't ever fill them), crisp the skins nicely. Leftover seasoning can be added just before serving, if desired.

I have made these countless times and I started omitting boiling them first. I cut them in half and roast them in a bit of olive oil, flip them when they start to crisp then smash them and add the sauce and parmesean and cook them a little longer. Less time consuming and less dirty dishes. I make them a lot more often now. They are definitely a family favorite.

These are really delicious. Hubby gives 5 stars, I give 4, only because I'm not sold on the addition of balsamic. (I think would be 5 stars without that). The key is to use small, yellow potatoes. You can skip putting them in a towel if you drain them and put them back into the hot pan to sit for a few minutes to dry out.

These tasted great though I used a pre-mixed herb rather than the individual herbs listed. I like this recipe better than making the smashed potatoes in oil on the stove as this is less messy. Granted, it is also a little less crispy. Another change I made was to cook the potatoes in chicken broth (I would have preferred vegetable broth but I didn't have any) instead of plain water. Just realized I also forgot to use the balsamic vinegar! Bet that would have made them even better:)
Very tasty and flavorful. I used Potato Inspirations Celebration Blend bite-size. Perfect. I might cook just a little bit longer for more crispiness next time.

I love making smashed potatoes. I totally cheat though. I find it is much easier to just put the potatoes in a microwave. I let them cool then transfer to a baking dish and smash them. My second cheat is to used garlic infused olive oil. There's no chance of burning the garlic that way. You get the right amount of garlic taste this way. I use whatever fresh herbs I have on hand.

Very good potato side dish. You can make the boiling step ahead and 30 minutes before dinner finish the recipe.
I didn't have all the herbs it calls for, but it still came out delicious. For people that were bothered by the dried rosemary, just crushed it little bit with your fingers before using it..

I used my regular russet potatoes I had on hand boiled mashed then spread a mixture of onion,garlic,balsamic,olive oil, thyme, rosemary,basil and chopped up patties of vegan meat and some oats too. Baked and came out so delicious.

I made these last night with a bag of Trader Joe's Potatoes/Baby Medley (the bag was 28 ounces and included a mix of baby red, yellow and purple potatoes). They were absolutely DELICIOUS! My husband loved them, too and we can't wait to have them again. I cut the potatoes in half, boiled for 20 minutes as directed, and let cool. Then I added them to the olive oil/butter/seasonings mixture in a bowl and tossed to coat well. From there, I placed the potatoes on the cooking sheet, smashed and drizzled any remaining mixture over them. Really yummy! The blend of seasonings is so good! Next time I think I am going to smash them before coating in the bowl.
Small changes I made: I used about 4tsp butter, cut them like a baked potato and squeezed them open, topped them with sauce and baked them 30 minutes... best potatoes I've had in a very long time.

These potatoes are not that appetizing to look at but taste good. The balsamic vinegar gives them an earthy tartness which wakes up your taste buds. If you want them crispy, however, you will need to bake them for much longer and make sure you smash them very thin.
I've tried this recipe a couple of times, it's easy and turns out great every time.

The herbed oil for this recipe is WONDERFUL. I used some of my aged balsamic vinegar which put it over the top. The little bit of the dregs of the oil leftover was enjoyed as added "garnish" and we soaked up every last bit!
I think the basic recipe is terrific for adding tweaks. My only suggestion is to boil the potatoes in a balsamic vinegar and water mix.

Not bad but not sure if it's worth the effort to make again. Make sure you cook them long enough to get plenty crispy as I think that was a mistake on my part. Just not sure how much I loved the balsamic vinegar. Might try again and use less
